newsitem.title: GERMANY: DB-Soft wants nominal share price halved.
newsitem.headline: DB-Soft wants nominal share price halved.

text.p: German software group DB-Soft AG wants its shareholders to decide to reduce the nominal worth of its shares to 25 marks ($16.43) from 50 marks, the German newsletter Bundesanzeiger reported on Thursday.
The largely-privately held software maker said on October 8 that it had lost half of its capital, forcing it to call a meeting of shareholders and its management board to resign.
The general meeting of shareholders which was held on February 6 should be repeated on November 29, the newsletter reported the company as saying.
The company's shares are traded on the Munich stock exchange and they closed dealing on Wednesday at 21 marks.
